title: How to find cursor on Mac: quick tips for locating your pointer easily
metaTitle: How to find cursor on Mac: Quick Tips
description: Lost your pointer? Learn how to find cursor on Mac using the built-in Shake to Locate feature and persistent accessibility settings for better visibility.
intro: To find your cursor on a Mac, you can use the built-in Shake to Locate feature or adjust persistent visibility settings in macOS. If you lose track of your pointer, quickly move your mouse back and forth or swipe your finger rapidly across the trackpad to make it temporarily enlarge.
tldr: Move your mouse or trackpad rapidly to activate Shake to Locate.
Enable permanent cursor enlargement in System Settings under Accessibility.
Use custom pointer colors to improve contrast against your background.
Restart your Mac or switch apps if the cursor vanishes entirely.

blocks.text: Using Shake to Locate on macOS

The fastest way to find cursor on Mac is the Shake to Locate feature. Introduced in macOS 10.11 El Capitan, this function is active by default on most modern systems. When you move your mouse back and forth quickly, the cursor grows significantly in size for a few seconds. This visual cue helps you pinpoint its exact location on your screen. If you have multiple monitors, this is especially helpful for identifying which display currently holds your pointer.

If shaking does not provide enough help, you can make your cursor permanently larger or change its color. This is useful for users with vision impairments or those working on high resolution displays where the standard cursor size feels too small. You can manage these settings within the System Settings app.

items: Open the Apple menu in the top left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click on the Accessibility tab located in the sidebar.
Select Display from the list of options on the right.
Scroll down to the Pointer section to find your customization tools.

blocks.text: Within the Pointer section, you will see a slider for pointer size. Moving this slider to the right increases the size of the cursor. You can also adjust the pointer outline color and the fill color. Changing these to high contrast colors, like bright yellow or white with a black outline, makes the cursor stand out against dark or busy desktop backgrounds.
Sometimes the cursor may disappear entirely. This can happen due to app glitches, software conflicts, or system freezes. If you cannot see your pointer, try these steps to restore it.

items: Switch to another app using Command plus Tab to see if the cursor reappears.
Open Mission Control to refresh your display windows.
Check if your third party mouse drivers are updated or conflicting with macOS.
Restart your Mac to clear temporary system memory glitches.
Disconnect your mouse or trackpad and reconnect it to refresh the connection.

blocks.text: Accessibility is a core component of the modern computing experience. With 7 percent of working age adults facing severe dexterity difficulties, simple navigation tools are essential. When you find cursor on Mac easily, you reduce the physical strain of hunting for a tiny object on a large screen. This is a small but meaningful step toward a more comfortable daily workflow.

faq.question: Can I turn off the Shake to Locate feature?
faq.answer: Yes. Navigate to System Settings, click Accessibility, then Display. You can toggle the Shake mouse pointer to locate switch to the off position.

faq.question: Why does my cursor get bigger when I move it fast?
faq.answer: That is the Shake to Locate feature working as intended. It is designed to help you find your cursor quickly if you lose track of it.

faq.question: Does changing cursor size affect performance?
faq.answer: No. Changing the pointer size or color has no impact on your Mac system performance or battery life.
